1.title: Cléebourg: A Northern Enclave Isolated by 90 km
1.html:
Cléebourg lies at the northern tip of Bas-Rhin, near Wissembourg, within the Vosges du Nord nature park. This vineyard was historically part of a continuous belt of vine growing stretching from southern Alsace all the way to the German Palatinate, until in the first half of the 20th century the continuous belt was cut, leaving Cléebourg about 90 km from the main Alsace vineyard belt as an isolated enclave.

After the Second World War, in 1946, the villagers founded a cooperative winery (cave coopérative), using war reparations as capital to rebuild the vineyard together. Today Cléebourg is an independent area of about 200 ha, with a climate cooler than its southern neighbours and less affected by spring frost, suited to white wines with elegant acidity and a fresh, delicate style — especially Riesling, which shows excellent quality after 2–3 years of ageing.

Since 1988, local growers have specially marked out 10 "lieux-dits" of high potential (such as Keimberg, Hannesacker and Kammerberg), giving them extra care and gradually developing their own "quasi-Grand Cru" spirit. Across the area the main varieties are Pinot Blanc Auxerrois (early-ripening, adapted to the local climate) and Pinot Gris, which together account for 54% of the planted area.
2.title: Klevener de Heiligenstein: A Complementary Geographical Indication Starring Savagnin rose
2.html:
Remember the Klevener de Heiligenstein mentioned in Level 1? It is the non-aromatic variant of Gewurztraminer — called "Heiligensteiner Klevner" in Alsace, it is Savagnin rose (non-musqué).

This variety was introduced to Heiligenstein (Bas-Rhin) in 1742. It is one of the complementary geographical indications of AOC Alsace, with Savagnin rose as the only authorised variety — limited to the immediately neighbouring villages of Bourgheim, Gertwiller, Goxwiller, Heiligenstein and Obernai.

In style: a dry white, restrained and reserved, with frankincense, spice and floral notes revealing its kinship with Gewurztraminer, yet more refined and delicately balanced — combining the vitality of Riesling with the richness of Pinot Gris, an excellent all-meal pairing wine that also suits some Asian dishes.
3.question: Why is the Cléebourg area about 90 km from the main Alsace vineyard belt, forming an isolated enclave?
3.options.1: It was historically part of a continuous belt of vine growing, which was cut in the first half of the 20th century, leaving Cléebourg isolated in the north
3.options.2: Because the local climate is completely unsuited to vines
3.options.3: Because Cléebourg is a newly developed area
3.explanation: Cléebourg was historically part of a continuous belt of vine growing stretching from southern Alsace all the way to the German Palatinate. In the first half of the 20th century this belt was cut for various reasons, leaving Cléebourg about 90 km from the main Alsace vineyard belt as a geographically isolated enclave — yet after the war the villagers (founding a cooperative in 1946) worked to rebuild and continue the winemaking tradition here.
